scope: Primary-method and author-code review only; no author environment installed, no model executed, no GPU used, no recommendation benefit established.

sources.title: Axial Attention in Multidimensional Transformers
sources.commit_basis: Latest commit returned for path=axial on review date; source fetched at this immutable repository commit.

files_read.inspection: Entry points and model wrapper located; architecture conclusions rely on transformers.py, not this wrapper.

verified: Attention operates on one tensor axis at a time.
Author code uses pre-normalized residual attention and MLP blocks.
Full image generative model additionally uses causal masks and shifts.
transfer_limits: Full receptive field is not equivalence to one dense attention layer.
History-time and SID-position axes require task-specific masking.
Independent centroid numbering does not supply natural cross-book grid alignment.

sources.title: MaxViT: Multi-Axis Vision Transformer
sections_read: Appendix A.1 MaxViT Block and Algorithm 1
sources.commit_basis: main commit resolved with GitHub API; immutable source fetched separately from the web tool's cached main view.
verified: Local window attention is followed by sparse global grid attention in the main block.
Grid groups have fixed G squared tokens; the number of groups grows with spatial resolution.
MaxViT includes MBConv and FFNs; it is not identical to axial row/column attention.
transfer_limits: Four code positions do not justify copying square 7-by-7 image windows.
Image ablation rankings are not recommendation performance evidence.
Linear attention-pair complexity assumes fixed group size; projection and FFN costs remain.

sources.title: Grid-Attention: Enhancing Computational Efficiency of Large Vision Models without Fine-Tuning
sources.author_provenance: Repository is explicitly linked in the official ECVA paper, page 2.
sources.commit_basis: main commit verified with commits/main API, then source read at immutable commit.
verified: Grid Clustering uses reshape and permutation rather than averaging or k-means.
S squared lower-resolution subimages retain the total number of tokens.
The inspected SAM block shuffles grouping during training and uses fixed grouping at inference.
Paper describes shuffle/deformable variants to reduce fixed-grid isolation.
transfer_limits: Vision spatial redundancy does not establish redundant or exchangeable codebook centroids.
Fixed S retains quadratic attention cost in token count, improving a factor S squared.
The note derives QK-transpose and attention-times-V costs from standard matrix shapes instead of propagating the paper's printed cubic HW matmul expression.
No performance-preserving training-free claim is transferred to recommendation.

sources.title: Universal Transformers
sources.commit_basis: master commit resolved with GitHub API, immutable utility implementation fetched.
verified: Recurrence is over depth, not an RNN over sequence positions.
Core weights are reused across refinement steps; position and step signals are available.
Fixed-step and adaptive-halting variants are distinct implementations.
transfer_limits: Parameter sharing does not remove repeated forward computation.
Changing per-request activations is different from changing global quantizer centroids.
ACT theoretical conditional computation does not guarantee practical GPU latency reduction.

local_code_checked.finding: Existing CrossPSECodebookMixer flattens global M-by-K centroids into one MHA sequence. This is not the proposed L-by-M history activation grid.

derived_not_paper_claims: Applying axial attention to the L-by-M history codeword grid.
Combining shared-depth loop with axial codeword attention.
Complexity examples at L=50, M=4 and M=4, K=256.
Code-index permutation sanity checks and task-specific stability controls.
